successors.note: Cliopatria's Viking settlements row covers East Anglia 870-877 and its Danelaw row from 878 (the infobox has 'Danelaw 869-918'); the kingdom 'was absorbed into England in 918' (Wessex annexed 918).

capitals.name: Dunwich (see of Felix; no capital named)
capitals.note: The page names no capital. It says Sigeberht 'oversaw the establishment of the first East Anglian see for Felix of Burgundy at Dommoc, probably Dunwich'; the dot is a placeholder for the kingdom's chief centre.

keyframe_review.note: 534-665, 12,391 km2. Cliopatria's outline reaches about 2,000 km2 (8-9 cells) south of the Stour into north Essex, which the page makes the East Saxon frontier ('The River Stour historically divided it from the East Saxons to the south') and the Kingdom of Essex page counts as East Saxon (Colchester); that part is removed. The infobox gives no area; the corrected shape is about 10,400 km2. The page: 'It comprised the territory which now constitutes the English counties of Norfolk and Suffolk'. Penda's wars (early 640s, 654) and Rædwald's overlordship (616) change no outline in the page.

ledger.note: 6th century: the kingdom of the East Angles forms under the Wuffingas. Infobox 'Established: 6th century'; 'Wehha listed as the first king of the East Angles', followed by Wuffa. The page gives no year, so 534 is Cliopatria's start, the year its Anglo-Saxon England row ends.

ledger.note: 794: Offa of Mercia executes Æthelberht and takes East Anglia. 'In 794, Offa of Mercia had the East Anglian king Æthelberht executed and then took control of the kingdom for himself'; infobox: client state of Mercia 794-796. The Offa page quotes the Chronicle: 'King Offa ordered King Æthelberht's head to be struck off'. The vassal's record: the counterpart is the overlord.

ledger.note: 796: East Anglia revives after Offa's death. Infobox: independent 796 to c. 799; Eadwald's revival after Offa died in 796 'was suppressed by the new Mercian king, Coenwulf'.

region.text: the English counties of Norfolk and Suffolk, 'perhaps the eastern part of the Fens', west to the Ouse, Lark and Kennett and at most the Cam

ledger.note: c. 799: Coenwulf of Mercia suppresses Eadwald and East Anglia is a Mercian client again. The infobox gives 'client state of Mercia ... c. 799-825'; the page does not date the suppression more closely.

region.text: the English counties of Norfolk and Suffolk, 'perhaps the eastern part of the Fens', west to the Ouse, Lark and Kennett and at most the Cam

ledger.note: 825: East Anglia rises against Mercia. 'East Anglian independence was restored by a rebellion against Mercia led by Æthelstan in 825'; Beornwulf of Mercia was defeated and killed, and his successor Ludeca died in 827. The Ellendun page has Beornwulf's defeat 'emboldened the East Angles to revolt'.

region.text: Thetford, where the army 'spent the winter of 865-866'

ledger.note: 865: the Great Heathen Army lands in East Anglia. 'The invaders initially landed in East Anglia, where King Edmund provided them with horses'; 'They spent the winter of 865-866 at Thetford'. A peace, not a conquest; the East Anglians kept the kingdom.

region.text: Thetford, where the army 'spent the winter of 865-866'

ledger.note: 866: the army marches north. It left 'towards the end of 866', capturing York in November 866; Cliopatria's 866 cut of east Anglian land for the Vikings is not supported by the page.

869: the Great Army conquers East Anglia and kills Edmund. 'In 869, the Great Army returned to East Anglia, conquering it and killing its king'; the army 'spent the winter of 869-870 at Thetford'. The Kingdom of East Anglia infobox has 'Danelaw 869-918'.

wars.name: Mercian wars against East Anglia under Penda
wars.outcome: 'In the early 640s, Penda defeated and killed both Ecgric and Sigeberht'; Anna and his son Jurmin were killed in 654 at the Battle of Bulcamp; in 655 Æthelhere of East Anglia joined Penda against Oswiu at the Winwaed.
wars.note: The page records no land changing hands and the infobox keeps East Anglia independent to 794. 640 is the start of the page's 'early 640s'.

wars.name: Battle of the River Idle
wars.outcome: Rædwald 'was strong enough to defeat and kill the Northumbrian king Æthelfrith at the Battle of the River Idle' in 616.
wars.note: Bede calls Rædwald overlord of the kingdoms south of the Humber and the Chronicle names him Bretwalda; undated, so not a ledger event.

wars.name: Offa's conquest of East Anglia

zones.text: the English counties of Norfolk and Suffolk, 'perhaps the eastern part of the Fens', west to the Ouse, Lark and Kennett and at most the Cam

wars.outcome: Offa had Æthelberht executed in 794 and took control of the kingdom; the Offa page has Æthelberht rebelling. Eadwald's revival after 796 was suppressed by Coenwulf.

wars.name: East Anglian revolt against Mercia
wars.outcome: Æthelstan's rebellion of 825 restored independence; Beornwulf was defeated and killed and Ludeca died in 827; 'The East Angles appealed to Egbert of Wessex for protection against the Mercians.'
wars.note: Beornwulf had just been beaten by Ecgberht at Ellendun (September 825).

wars.name: Great Heathen Army in East Anglia
wars.outcome: The army wintered at Thetford in 865-866 on a peace bought with horses, and returned in 869, conquering East Anglia and killing Edmund.
wars.note: After 879 'the Vikings settled permanently in East Anglia' under Guthrum (reigned to 890).

certainty.note: The page gives county-scale limits (Stour, Ouse, Lark, Kennett, the Cam at most) but no treaty or survey line; the Fen edge is the softest.

notes: Cliopatria's East Anglia shapes all include about 8-9 cells of north Essex south of the Stour; they are trimmed by minus admin1 Essex (the Kingdom of Essex dossier adds the same cells). The 866-869 shape's 8-cell Thetford cut for the Viking settlements is not supported: the army wintered at Thetford in 865-866 and left. The page's status line is 'Independent (6th century-794; 796-c. 799; 825-869)' with client-state spans for Mercia; 799-825 is bridged in the keyframe 800. The page gives no founding year (534 is Cliopatria's start, confidence 1), no capital, no area and no king list with reign years, so rulers are omitted. Rædwald's overlordship south of the Humber (Bede) is undated on the page and not a ledger event; the appeal to Egbert of Wessex in 825 is not recorded as a protectorate because the infobox keeps East Anglia independent. Mirror events needed in other dossiers: Mercia (vassal 794-796 and c. 799-825 with counterpart kingdom-of-east-anglia), viking-settlements (occupation 865-866 and the 869 gain), danelaw (the land from 878). Page budget: East Anglia plus Great Heathen Army plus the shared Offa and Ellendun pages.
